Recorded. Fourth question.

**Question:** How should the JSON export be laid out — as one long line or indented across several — and should non-English characters appear as themselves or as escape codes? (FR-020)

**Why it matters:** SC-006 promises exports round-trip "with no value altered", so tests will compare output text directly; without a fixed layout a title like `Café` could come out as `Caf\u00e9` in one run and `Café` in another, and both would look defensible.

**Recommended:** Option A — two-space indentation with non-English characters written literally as UTF-8. The output stays valid JSON for any parser, reads sensibly when a user just looks at it, and a title shows the same characters the user typed rather than escape codes.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Two-space indented, one record per block, non-ASCII characters literal UTF-8, single trailing newline |
| B | One compact line, no spaces, non-ASCII characters literal UTF-8, single trailing newline |
| C | One compact line with non-ASCII escaped as `\uXXXX` (the language's default behaviour) |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (<=5 words) |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
